seo.meta_title: What Is Outback's Bloomin' Onion? Price, Calories & Sauce
seo.meta_description: The Bloomin' Onion is Outback's giant battered, fried onion cut to open like a flower, served with spicy Bloomin' sauce. Price, calories and how it started.

question: What Is Outback's Bloomin' Onion?
quick_answer: The Bloomin' Onion is Outback Steakhouse's signature appetizer: a whole large onion cut so it opens like a flower, then battered, seasoned, deep-fried and served with Outback's spicy Bloomin' dipping sauce. It has been on the menu since Outback opened in 1988. It is meant for sharing, costs roughly $10 to $13 depending on location, and Outback lists it at around 1,900 calories.
key_facts: A whole onion cut into petals, battered and fried
Served with Outback's creamy, spicy Bloomin' sauce
On the menu since Outback opened in 1988
Roughly $10 to $13; price set by location
About 1,900 calories, so it's best shared

body.heading: What the Bloomin' Onion is
body.text: The Bloomin' Onion is a whole large onion that is cut from the top into dozens of wedges, but not all the way through, so it opens up like a flower. It is then coated in seasoned batter and deep-fried until the petals are crispy. It comes to the table whole, with a cup of dipping sauce in the center, and everyone pulls off petals to dip.

body.heading: What the dipping sauce is
body.text: The dipping sauce is a creamy, spicy sauce that Outback calls its Bloomin' sauce. Outback has not shared the recipe, and copycat versions usually build it from mayonnaise, ketchup or chili sauce, horseradish and cayenne. Outback uses the same sauce on other Bloomin' items, like its Bloomin' Fried Chicken and the Bloomin' Burger.

body.heading: How much it costs
body.text: Outback sets prices by location, so the Bloomin' Onion usually costs somewhere around $10 to $13 before tax, and more on delivery apps. Back in 1994, an Outback menu listed it at $4.95. Even after inflation, the price has gone up a bit faster than you might expect.

body.heading: Bloomin' Onion calories
body.text: Outback's own menu lists the Bloomin' Onion at around 1,900 calories, which is close to a full day's worth for many adults. That is why most people treat it as a starter for three or four people rather than a snack for one. For the calories of other Outback dishes, see our Outback menu page or try our calorie calculator.

body.heading: A bit of history
body.text: Outback Steakhouse opened in 1988 with an Australian theme, and the Bloomin' Onion was on the menu from the start. It quickly became the chain's best-known dish, and many restaurants now serve their own blooming onions. Outback has also spun it into limited-time items over the years, such as a Loaded Bloomin' Onion topped with cheese fries.

faqs.q: What is a Bloomin' Onion made of?
faqs.a: A whole large onion cut into petals, coated in seasoned batter and deep-fried, served with a spicy dipping sauce.

faqs.q: How much is a Bloomin' Onion at Outback?
faqs.a: Roughly $10 to $13 depending on location, and more on delivery apps.

faqs.q: How many calories are in a Bloomin' Onion?
faqs.a: Outback lists it at around 1,900 calories, so it is usually shared.

faqs.q: What sauce comes with the Bloomin' Onion?
faqs.a: Outback's Bloomin' sauce, a creamy, spicy dip. The recipe is secret.

faqs.q: How many people does a Bloomin' Onion feed?
faqs.a: It is built for sharing and works well as a starter for three or four people.
